To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the charge collection in n–in– n detectors is higher than in p–in–n ones for the same irradiation fluence.

(i) the CCE is significantly improved when n-side rather than the p–side is read out; (ii) the charge sharing properties are preserved up to fluences where the n–in-n detector is fully depleted and (iii) the use of oxygen enriched silicon substrats is viable up to the highest fluence of 1.2×10 15 proton cm − 2.

the n–in-n read out geometry has the highest CCE at the highest irradiation dose, and that the charge collection efficiency of the n–in--n detectors is not significantly affected by the transverse component of space charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation hardness of silicon microstrip detectors and the development of new detector technologies to meet the requirements of the future high energy physics experiments.
the development of silicon strip detectors that are suitable for use in the high radiation environments of the LHC.
the optimization of the detector design for future experiments in high energy physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the n–in n detector geometry can be used up to fluences in the order of 10 14 proton cm −2, and possibly higher, for high resolution tracking in the ATLAS inner detector at the LHC.
the use of n–in– n detectors for tracking applications at the HL– LHC is feasible.
the charge collection efficiency of n–in– n detectors is higher than that of p–in–n devices at high irradiation doses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxygenated n–n detectors are the preferred option for the read-out in the ATLAS pixel and strip detectors at the HL-LHC.
the CCE of oxygenated n-bulk detectors is comparable to that of p-bulk detectors at high fluences.
the n–in –n detectors are the best solution for high radiation environments, such as those found in the inner tracker at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the n–in-n geometry is a promising option for the construction of highly segmented, high radiation tolerance detectors.
oxygenated n–side read out detectors can be used for the construction of tracking detectors at high luminosity hadron colliders.

oxygen enriched n–in– n detectors can be operated at low voltage and at high radiation doses with a CCE of 98% or higher, which is a requirement for a number of applications, such as the ATLAS upgrade.
